_comment: Roster for /vr-youtubers. This page is a directory: who covers what, and where to find them. It deliberately does NOT publish or comment on whether a creator is currently posting, how often they post, or when they last uploaded. lastUpload and lastVerified are kept here for our own maintenance pass only (confirming a channel still exists and the handle still resolves) and must never be rendered on the page. Subscriber and video counts were read from each channel's own page on lastVerified.

creators.name: Nathie
creators.note: The biggest generalist in VR video and the best single starting point if you only follow one channel. Broad Quest and PC VR coverage, hands-on first looks, and a habit of crediting the people whose footage he features. His post on the WinlatorXR Half-Life 2 result is what carried that story to a mass audience.

creators.name: Naysy
creators.note: Tests the question you actually have rather than the one that makes a better thumbnail. "Can The Steam Machine Run VR Games?" and "Does VR work on Steam Machine?" are two separate passes at the same hardware problem, which is the kind of follow-through most coverage skips.

creators.name: ThisKory
creators.note: The smallest English channel here and one of the most useful. His Weekly VR News format rounds up the beat in one sitting, and he writes real setup walkthroughs alongside it, like the UEVR guide for Halo: Campaign Evolved.

creators.name: Beardo Benjo
creators.note: The modding channel. Cyberpunk 2077 VR, Mirror's Edge VR, BioShock Infinite VR. If a flat game has picked up a VR layer, this is usually the best place to see what it actually looks like before you commit an evening to installing it.

creators.name: Gamertag VR
creators.note: One of the deepest game libraries on this page, spanning Quest, PSVR2, and PC VR. Reviews land in a blunt buy, wait for a sale, or ignore verdict, which is more useful than a number out of ten.

creators.name: Without Parole
creators.note: The PlayStation VR2 specialist, with a catalogue that runs to thousands of videos on that platform alone. Reviews, trailers, and a podcast. PSVR2 owners get left out of a lot of general VR coverage, and this is the fix.

creators.name: Cas and Chary XR
creators.note: Headset and smart glasses reviews from a duo willing to question the category rather than just rate the products, which is where a title like "Maybe We've Been Building Headsets Wrong" comes from. They renamed the channel from Cas and Chary VR to Cas and Chary XR, which is the industry's whole shift compressed into one letter.

creators.name: MRTV
creators.note: One of the longest-running headset review channels anywhere, and the one most willing to argue that a cheap headset beats an expensive one. The URXR One review makes the case that a $799 device matters more than Vision Pro.

creators.name: Tyriel Wood
creators.note: Go here for smart glasses specifically: VITURE Pro 2, XREAL DNA, and a 30 day wear test comparing the camera-free Memomind One against Even G2. He lives with the hardware before reviewing it, which is rarer than it sounds.

creators.name: BMFVR
creators.note: Mixed reality is the specialty, and the production care shows. "This is what mixed reality on Quest 3 was ACTUALLY meant to be" is a good sample of the register: enthusiastic, but built on a real demo rather than a spec sheet.

creators.name: ThrillSeeker
creators.note: The most quotable essayist VR video has produced. Pieces like "The VR Industry's Great Reset" and his CES roundups treat the medium as something worth arguing about rather than just unboxing. Start with the essays, not the reviews.

creators.name: Virtual Reality Oasis
creators.note: A deep library of Quest headset reviews and app roundups that remains one of the better places to research a headset you are thinking about buying. He also built and shipped the Ready Or Not VR mod, so the channel doubles as a record of someone crossing from covering VR to making it.

creators.name: SadlyItsBradley
creators.note: One of the central figures in XR hardware leaks, with a long record on unreleased Valve and Meta hardware. Worth following on X as well as YouTube, since a lot of the detail work happens there in threads.

creators.name: Syrmor
creators.note: Interviews strangers inside VRChat and edits the results into short documentaries, and the best of them are the strongest record anywhere of what social VR is actually like for the people living in it. Nothing else on this page is doing this.

creators.name: Fix My Oculus
creators.note: The practical channel, and the closest match here to the standard we hold ourselves to: tell people how to actually run the thing. Hardware repairs, PCVR streaming comparisons, and guides like "I Made My Quest 3 Run Steam Games Without a PC."

creators.name: OtterWorldly
creators.note: VR fitness treated as a routine instead of a novelty, which is rarer than it should be. Beat Saber runs in mixed reality, rowing machines wired up as controllers, and a general willingness to show what sustained play looks like rather than a first session.

creators.name: Valem Tutorials
creators.note: The Unity VR tutorial channel, including a multi-part series on building a VR multiplayer game that runs from network setup through distributed authority and ownership. Note this is the tutorials channel; the main @ValemVR handle is a separate, mostly short-form feed.

creators.name: Dilmer Valecillos
creators.note: XR development with the AI tooling angle taken seriously rather than as a gimmick. He built and shipped a VR/MR game with AI assistance in 30 days and documented it, and tests things like Unity's CLI against Codex rather than just describing them.

creators.name: Virtumaniacos
creators.note: The largest VR-focused channel we found anywhere, by a factor of more than four over the biggest English one, and effectively invisible in English-language VR coverage. Game-led and genuinely fun. If you think of VR video as an English-speaking scene, this is the entry that should change your mind.

creators.name: VoodooDE VR (English)
creators.note: A German creator who owns close to every headset that has shipped and runs a separate English-language channel for the rest of us. The catalogue runs to thousands of videos, including practical pieces like using a Steam Machine plus Quest 3 as a Steam Frame alternative.

creators.name: Okurasu VR
creators.note: A second-cohort Meta Quest ambassador and the first DPVR ambassador, covering the Japanese Quest scene. Digs into corners English coverage tends to skip, like HeyVR.io and free WebXR games that run with no install at all.

creators.name: SideBook VR
creators.note: 568 subscribers and a library in the hundreds, which tells you why this page is not ordered by size. Ran the Half-Life 2 Quest 3 standalone test three days before that story reached a large audience, plus a Portal 1 test alongside it. The best argument here that audience and contribution are different things.
